standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the conclusion "s is not weakly associated to f_* F" into the explicit statement that no nonzero element m of the stalk has all a_i^n m equal to zero.

core_obligations: Base change the morphism along g : Spec(O_{S,s}) -> S, denote f' : X' -> Spec(O_{S,s}) the result and g' : X' -> X the other projection, and identify the stalk of f_* F at s with (g^* f_* F)_s and then with (f'_* (g')^* F)_s, using that g induces an isomorphism on local rings at s and then flat base change (proof lines 728-738).
Reduce to the case where S = Spec(A) is the spectrum of a local ring (A, m) and s is the closed point: the point s of Spec(O_{S,s}) is still not in the image of f' (proof lines 738-740).

Write f_* F as the quasi-coherent sheaf associated to an A-module M, and use that s is not in the image of f to exhibit X = union over a in m of f^{-1} D(a) as an open covering; by quasi-compactness of X extract a_1, ..., a_n in m with X = f^{-1}D(a_1) union ... union f^{-1}D(a_n) (proof lines 741-747).

Deduce that M -> M_{a_1} + ... + M_{a_n} is injective, hence that for every nonzero element m of the stalk at the maximal ideal there is an index i with a_i^n m nonzero for all n >= 0, which is exactly the statement that m is not weakly associated to M (proof lines 748-753).
proof_roadmap: Flat base change to Spec(O_{S,s}) to make the base local (proof lines 728-740).
Replacement of f_* F by the A-module M and construction of the finite cover of X by the opens f^{-1}D(a_i) with a_i in the maximal ideal (proof lines 741-747).
Injectivity of M into the product of the localisations and the resulting annihilation criterion, giving that the maximal ideal is not weakly associated to M (proof lines 748-753).
difficulty_reason: The claim is that if f : X -> S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and s is not in the image of f, then s is not weakly associated to f_* F (statement lines 721-724). The proof has two steps that are not routine. First a flat base change to Spec(O_{S,s}) reduces the problem to a local base (A, m) with s the closed point, using that base change by a morphism that is an isomorphism on the local ring at s does not change the stalk (proof lines 728-740). Second, the hypothesis that s is outside the image is converted into the open covering X = union over a in m of f^{-1}D(a), from which quasi-compactness extracts finitely many a_1, ..., a_n in the maximal ideal with M -> M_{a_1} + ... + M_{a_n} injective (proof lines 741-748). That injectivity is precisely what rules out an element of the stalk annihilated by a power of every a_i, i.e. what rules out weak associatedness (proof lines 748-753). This is H2: the covering indexed by the maximal ideal and its finite refinement are the non-formal content, but no Noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is needed and each step is short.

dedup.scope: Targeted neighbours only: public items about weakly associated points, weak assassins and pushforwards, in particular those from flat.tex and more-morphisms.tex; the retired-claims list; the preparation worklist; the pool card operations/pool-cards/stacks-divisors.json and the Stacks tags 0AVN and 0CUQ. No global novelty claim.
compared: public 1937 (tag 05IG, flat-lemma-weak-bourbaki-pre) is the tensor formula for weakly associated primes over a finitely presented flat algebra, and public 1510 (tag 05IK, flat-theorem-finite-type-flat) is the openness of the finite-type flat locus under a finitely-many-weak-assassins hypothesis; both are structural results about weak assassins of tensor products, and neither concerns the pushforward of a quasi-coherent module along a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism or the location of weakly associated points relative to the image of the morphism.

public 467 (tag 0GSI) and public 470 (tag 05F1) are about relative associated points of finite-type or flat morphisms and their behaviour under specialisation and generic flatness; they do not use weak assassins and do not prove that a point outside the image fails to be weakly associated.

The present card is deliberately not opened together with the companion lemma of the same chapter, lemma-ass-functorial-equal (source lines 834-877), which merely chains three inclusions, one of which is the present lemma; nor with lemma-depth-2-hartog, whose proof is a two-line appeal to the present lemma together with the weakly-associated support lemma.
